title: Regenerated sprites.json order no longer matches sprites.odin's positional bbox binding
evidence: tools/gen_sprites.py main(): `build_flat("small_biz", SMALL_BIZ_FILL, SMALL_BIZ_SIZE, 1.20); names.append("small_biz")` / `build_flat("campus", CAMPUS_FILL, CAMPUS_SIZE, 1.95); names.append("campus")` / `for ports in (4, 8, 16): build_puck(ports, ...)` — then `json.dump({"res": RES, "order": names, "content_bbox": boxes}, f, indent=1)` emits order [..., dc, small_biz, campus, puck_1, puck_2, puck_3]. app/render/sprites.odin pins the opposite: `files := [SPRITE_COUNT]string{ "house_0", "house_1", "house_2", "house_3", "host", "dc", "puck_1", "puck_2", "puck_3", "small_biz", "campus", }` and binds positionally with no name check: `for i in 0..<SPRITE_COUNT { name, okn := order[i].(json.String) ... sh.bboxes[i][k] = f32(n) }`; `base := sh.bboxes[6][2]` is the puck tier base. The committed sprites.json still has the old order ("dc", "puck_1", "puck_2", "puck_3", "small_biz", "campus"), and docs/silhouette-spec.md §4 pins "11 sprites, fixed names/order (`sprites.odin` `SPRITE_COUNT :: 11`)" — while the new docstring says "Output: assets/sprites/{house_0..3, host, dc, small_biz, campus, puck_1..3}.png".
detail: Sidecar order no longer matches the renderer's pinned files[]; bboxes bind positionally with no name check, so the follow-up re-render trims five sprites wrongly and corrupts the bboxes[6] tier base — silent, then locked in by the T2 re-bless.
recommended_fix: Restore the pinned emission order: move the small_biz/campus build_flat calls after the puck loop in main() (pucks at indices 6-8), or assert order equals the renderer's 11-name sequence before writing sprites.json.

title: Spec §1 'ridge along the long axis' contradicts the shipped gable default (ridge along Y, the short axis)
evidence: docs/silhouette-spec.md:38: `- **Geometry:** flat gable rect — rect footprint, ridge along the long axis, the` (next line: `+X slope 10% darker (the two-tone ridge line is the house read).`). tools/gen_sprites.py:226 docstring: `"""Gable roof with the ridge along Y and a per-face tone split (the +X` and :239-240: `r1 = bm.verts.new((0, -hd, base_z + h))` / `r2 = bm.verts.new((0, hd, base_z + h))` — ridge spans ±hd (Y). With `HOUSE_SIZE     = (0.62, 0.56)   # gable rect` (bw > bd), Y is the SHORT axis.
detail: The fill-in-the-blanks doc the user sculpts against specifies a ridge orientation the default table cannot produce (ridge direction is hard-coded in add_gable, not a table knob); doc and default render disagree.
recommended_fix: Make doc and default agree: either rewrite §1 as 'ridge along Y (the short axis)' or swap HOUSE_SIZE to (0.56, 0.62) so the ridge truly runs along the long axis.

title: Outline-ring width stated as +0.03 in the README but +0.06 in spec §0 (code expands +0.06 total)
evidence: assets/blender/README.md:26: `| Outline | thin dark ink `#33414F` plate at the base, footprint + ~0.03 (≈2px in-game ring) |`. docs/silhouette-spec.md:29: `| Outline | thin dark ink plate `#33414F` at base, footprint + ~0.06 (≈2px in-game ring) | MM's defining edge |`. tools/gen_sprites.py: `OUTLINE_RING = 0.03   # ink ring width around the fill (scene units, ~2px in-game)` and add_outline: `add_cube(name + "_o", (cx, cy, OUTLINE_H / 2), (fw + 2 * OUTLINE_RING, fd + 2 * OUTLINE_RING, OUTLINE_H),` (total +0.06).
detail: Two new docs give different ring widths for the same outline while both claim '≈2px in-game ring'; a user sculpting to the README halves the ring the script ships.
recommended_fix: Pick one convention and state it identically in both docs: OUTLINE_RING 0.03 per side = footprint +0.06 total. Fix the README's '+0.03'.

title: Per-sprite camera pads sit outside the SPEC table; larger footprints clip at the frame edge undetected
evidence: tools/gen_sprites.py: `cd.ortho_scale = 1.9 * pad` (aim) with pads passed per call: `shot(sc, name, 1.12)` (house), `shot(sc, name, pad)` (build_flat; 1.20/1.60/1.20/1.95 from main()), `shot(sc, name, 0.95)` (puck — puck_3 fills 202/256px of the frame). docs/silhouette-spec.md §2: `edit the SPEC table in `tools/gen_sprites.py` (hexes, footprints, toggles) and re-run`. app/render/sprites.odin accepts edge-touching boxes: `if x < 0 || y < 0 || w <= 0 || h <= 0 || x + w > 256 || y + h > 256 {` (x=0 / x+w=256 pass).
detail: Pads are hidden second knobs absent from the fill-in-the-blanks surface; a user footprint increase overflows the fixed ortho frame and clips silently — no bbox range check catches edge clipping.
recommended_fix: Derive pad from the footprint (pad proportional to max extent) or add pads to the SPEC table; have content_bbox warn when content touches the canvas edge.
